name: Carve a simple wooden spoon
blurb: The classic green-woodworking project: an axe, a knife and a hook knife turn a branch into something you eat with every day.
gear: A sloyd knife and a hook knife
steps: Choose green wood, which cuts far more easily than seasoned timber, and split a blank along the grain rather than sawing across it.
Draw the spoon on the blank, aligning the bowl with the grain, and axe out the rough profile.
Refine the outside with the sloyd knife, working with the grain and using the four basic carving grips.
Hollow the bowl with the hook knife, cutting in from both sides towards the middle rather than gouging in one direction.
Refine the crank — the bend between handle and bowl — which is what makes a spoon comfortable to use.
Let it dry slowly in a paper bag, then finish with a final knife pass or fine sanding and food-safe oil.
tips: Drying too fast splits the bowl. A paper bag for a week slows it down.
Sharp tools do the work. Strop constantly; a blunt hook knife is dangerous and exhausting.
Cut with the grain, always. Tear-out in the bowl is very hard to fix.
proof: A spoon you actually use daily, comfortable in the hand and free of splits.
